newsitem.title: UK: Eastbound Feb W.Africa crude sales seen at mln bpd.
newsitem.headline: Eastbound Feb W.Africa crude sales seen at mln bpd.

text.p: West African crude exports to Asian-Pacific buyers will soar back above a million barrels a day (bpd) in February for the first time in a year, oil traders and shippers said on Monday.
"The Far East has taken a lot of barrels for February," said a trader. "There's been very strong interest."
China, Taiwan, Korea, Australia, the Philippines and India all figure as buyers for February, taking crudes from Nigeria, Gabon, Angola and the Congo.
South Korean refiners, now running new distillation capacity, are set to import particularly large volumes in February, traders said.
Lucky Goldstar, Caltex and Yukong are all slated to lift West African grades including Nigerian Forcados, Congolese Djeno and Gabonese Mandji.
Mobil is expected to take West African crude to Australia and Elf a cargo to the Philippines.
India bought almost six million barrels of Nigerian Qua Iboe in a tender for February sailing.
Eastbound West African shipments first broke a million barrels a day last February, petering out in early summer before surging again in July.
Dealers said extra refining capacity in the region and tighter emission standards for refined products has sparked growing demand for the low sulphur West African crudes.
